feedback: If a child draws the plant starting at the soil with no roots, pull the real plant up again and ask: 'What is holding it in the ground? What is under the soil?' Have them add the roots to their drawing.
Praise drawings that show roots spreading below a soil line and that label all four parts.
If a label is placed on the wrong part, point to the matching part on the real plant and ask the child to correct it.
activities.intendedInsight: A flowering plant has roots, stem, leaves and a flower; the roots are a real part of the plant even though they are usually hidden underground.
learnerActions: Observe a real flowering potted plant, then a small flowering weed or plant that has been pulled up so the roots are visible, rinsing soil off so the root system shows.
Point to and name each part out loud: roots, stem, leaves, flower.
Draw the whole plant from observation, including the roots below a soil line, and write or copy a label on each part.
Discuss which part is normally hidden and would be easy to forget (the roots).
activities.title: Pull up a real plant and draw a labelled diagram

feedback: If a child says a tree is not a plant, line up a small plant and a tree and show that both have roots, a stem (trunk) and leaves; a tree is a big plant.
If a child will not connect trunk and stem, point to each in turn and ask what job each does (both hold the plant up and carry water).
Confirm correct matches by restating: 'Yes — the trunk is the tree's stem.'
activities.intendedInsight: A tree has the same basic body plan as a small flowering plant — the trunk is a woody stem and branches are stems — so a tree is a big, woody plant.
learnerActions: Look at a small flowering plant and a tree side by side.
Match equivalent parts: the tree's trunk to the plant's stem, the tree's branches to stems, and the leaves and roots on both.
Say in your own words why a tree is a plant too, highlighting the trunk as 'a big woody stem'.
Name the tree parts: roots, trunk, branches, leaves.
activities.title: Map the tree onto the little plant

feedback: When a part is placed wrongly, it bounces back; prompt the child: 'Where does this one go — above or below the soil?'
Confirm a completed build by naming the parts together with the child.
If the child leaves out the roots, point to the empty underground space and ask what is missing.
activities.intendedInsight: The parts belong together as one organised plant, each in its own place; a small flowering plant and a tree are built from the same basic kinds of parts — roots, a stem (a woody trunk with branches on the tree) and leaves.
learnerActions: From a tray of part cards (roots, stem, leaves, flower), place each part in its correct position to assemble a whole plant.
Do the same for a tree (roots, trunk, branches, leaves).
Self-check: a misplaced part is returned so the child can try again.
After building, name each part placed.
activities.title: Build the plant from a parts tray

feedback: If a child names roots but says they only hold the plant up, explain that roots take in water from the soil as well as holding the plant steady. A celery stick stood in coloured water and left for several hours or overnight shows the colour travelling up the stalk, which is evidence that water moves up through a plant. A celery stick is a cut leaf stalk with no roots, so pair this with the pulled-up plant to help the child connect taking water in to the roots. Full understanding pairs naming with roots taking in water, not anchoring alone.
If a child treats the tree as a separate category, return to lining up the plant and tree and matching trunk to stem.

Extend: ask whether a cactus is a plant and what parts it has (roots, a thick green stem, and spines that are its unusual leaves; it also flowers, but only at certain times), to test transfer beyond typical leafy plants.
activities.intendedInsight: Secure naming and locating of parts on both a plant and a tree, tied to the first functions: roots take in water (and hold the plant steady) and leaves catch sunlight.
learnerActions: On a diagram of a whole plant with roots showing, point to and name the roots, stem, leaves and flower.
On a picture of a tree, point to and name the roots, trunk, branches and leaves.
Match each tree part to its flowering-plant equivalent.
Answer aloud: what is the job of the roots — what are they doing down in the soil? Which part catches the sunlight?
activities.title: Check: label the parts and say the root's job
